battle.name: 鳴條之戰
battle.brief: 公元前1675年，商湯率諸侯聯軍自亳出師，滅葛、韋、顧、昆吾之後壓向夏境，與桀的中央軍隊在晉南夏縣西的鳴條之野會戰。桀軍崩，桀走保三皐，湯追之再戰，桀奔車走，湯放桀於南巢，夏亡商興。陣上所見仍是裝在木柲上的青銅矛與戈，卡面埃及長矛並未隨軍而至。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 鳴條之戰是商湯滅夏的決定性野戰，交戰的一方是商族聯軍，另一方是夏朝的王師與被強行徵發的方國、部落之眾。商方以商族本部的武裝為骨幹：湯以亳為基地（亳的地望有數說，或指今河南商丘，或指今河南偃師一帶），任用伊尹整飭內部、經營盟國，先後翦除葛、韋、顧、昆吾等夏的衛星小國，把歷次征伐累積下來的聯盟編為伐夏的總體。《孟子·滕文公下》記「湯始征自葛，十一征而無敵於天下」，這句話說明商軍並非傾國一次出擊，而是長期征伐換來的聯盟作戰。最高指揮在湯本人，軍政由伊尹總攬，誓師、占卜與祭祀由商的巫史主持。夏方是桀（履癸）統治下的夏王朝中央武裝，王畿的常備師旅之外，附加了桀時期被鎮壓、被攤派的方國之眾；雙方共同的背景是青銅時代中期的中原，車、馬、弓矢、青銅戈矛與石斧都是共通的技術裝備，桀「奔車走」的記載說明車在夏軍之中份量不輕。問題在於夏的統治已到末路，《詩經·商頌·長發》所追述的商族在夏秩序中的從屬地位，說明商本不是與夏平起平坐的方國，而是被夏壓在下面的一支；到桀時，諸侯叛離、方國反側，夏的中央武力再強，也要在腹地以寡待眾，鳴條正是這樣的絕境中打開的。
countriesEn: The Battle of Mingtiao was the decisive field battle by which the Xia was destroyed, and the two sides were the Shang tribal confederacy on the one hand and, on the other, the royal troops of the Xia court together with the contingents of subject polities and tribes that Jie had called up by force. On the Shang side the armed body of the Shang people themselves formed the core. Tang made his base at Bo, a place variously identified with the neighbourhood of Shangqiu in Henan or with Yanshi in the same province, employed Yi Yin to set his own house in order and to manage his alliances, and in turn cut away the small satellite polities of Xia such as Ge, Wei, Gu and Kunwu, so that the force he brought against Xia was a coalition accumulated over a long series of campaigns. The Mengzi at Tengwen says that Tang began his campaigns at Ge and in eleven campaigns had no enemy left under heaven, which shows that the Shang army was not one desperate national effort but an alliance bought with long years of campaigning. The highest command lay with Tang himself, the war administration was in Yi Yin's hands, and the swearing of the oath, the divination and the sacrifices were conducted by the Shang ritual specialists. The Xia side was the central armed force of the Xia dynasty under Jie, whose standing troops of the royal domain were supplemented by the levies of the subject polities that Jie had repressed and taxed. The background common to both was the Central Plain in the middle of the Bronze Age, where the chariot, the horse, the bow, the bronze ge and spear and the stone axe were shared technology, and the record that Jie fled by chariot and on foot tells us that chariots carried no small weight in the Xia army. The difficulty was that Xia rule had reached its end, and the dependent position of the Shang people within the Xia order, as recounted in the Shang Odes of the Shijing in the Changfa, shows that the Shang were not a polity on equal footing with Xia but a branch held down beneath it. By the time of Jie the lords were leaving and the subject polities were turning; however strong the central Xia force was, it would have to meet a coalition in its own heartland with inferior numbers, and Mingtiao is precisely the battle fought out in such a desperate position.
people: 這場戰爭留下姓名的核心人物分屬三方。商湯（成湯，甲骨文或稱「大乙」，後世多稱其名為履）是商族領袖，也是本戰的統帥；《史記·夏本紀》記他在出師前「改正朔，易服色，上白，朝會以晝」，改曆法、改車服、改朝會的時辰，說明商方在號令與象徵體系上先行一步，而這一步本身就是戰前的準備。伊尹是商的宰相與軍師，《孟子·萬章上》記「湯三聘伊尹」，《尚書·說命上》保存的湯與伊尹問答則把這段君臣際遇寫成了後世君主的教科書；他與鳴條之戰的具體位置沒有早期文獻記載，但伐桀前的方國經略、聯軍的編組與出師時機，傳統上都歸在他名下，《史記·殷本紀》記太甲即位後伊尹放之於桐宮、自攝朝政，可見他在商初權力結構中的份量。夏方留下名字的是末代君主桀（履癸）與其臣佐：諫臣關龍逢因直言進諫被殺，豬存子、費侯伯一類的勸諫之臣也見於後世類書；至於西伯昌（後來的周文王），他在夏末商初之際已是商廷不得不留意的方國領袖，但他與鳴條之戰的關係沒有可靠記載，一般認為周人此時勢力尚弱，未見大舉出兵，只把夏的崩潰看作可以等待的機會。此外，先秦諸子反覆援引的湯誓之辭雖非戰爭當時的實錄，卻保存了誓師時「夏氏有罪」「予畏上帝，不敢不正」一類措辭，是研究商方如何自我說明此役最直接的材料；至於桀在戰陣中的表現，記載只剩下「奔車走」幾個動作，連他如何列陣、是否中流矢都無人記載。
peopleEn: The core of the named figures in this war comes from three sides. Tang of Shang, Cheng Tang, called Da Yi in the oracle bones and known in later ages by the personal name Lu, was the leader of the Shang people and the commander of this war. The Shiji in the annals of the House of Xia records that before setting out he corrected the calendar, changed the dress of the court, made white the colour above and moved the morning audience to daylight, changing the reckoning of time, the dress of the court and the hour of the assembly; this shows that the Shang had taken a step ahead in the matter of command and of the symbolic apparatus of rule, and that step was itself part of the preparations for the campaign. Yi Yin was the Shang chancellor and strategist. The Mengzi at Wanzhang says that Tang sought Yi Yin out three times, and the exchange between Tang and Yi Yin preserved in the Shangshu's Shuo Ming gives that meeting of ruler and minister the shape of a textbook for later sovereigns. His precise part in the battle of Mingtiao is not recorded in any early text, but the management of the subject polities before the war on Xia, the organisation of the coalition and the timing of the departure have traditionally been put to his account, and the Shiji in the annals of the House of Yin records how Yi Yin, after Taia had taken the throne, sent him into the Tong palace and assumed the government himself, which shows the weight he carried in the power structure of the early Shang. On the Xia side the names left are those of the last ruler Jie, known as Jue, and of his courtiers: the remonstrating minister Guan Longfeng was killed for speaking frankly, and men of the kind of Zhu Cunzi and Fei Houbo appear in the records of later class-books. As for Xibo Chang, the King Wen of Zhou to come, he was already at the end of the Xia and the beginning of the Shang a leader of a subject polity whom the Shang court could not afford to ignore, but his relation to the battle of Mingtiao is not reliably recorded; the general view is that the Zhou were still weak at that time and did not mount any large expedition, and simply watched the collapse of Xia as an opportunity to wait for. One further point: the words of the Tang Oath, quoted again and again by the pre-Qin writers, are not a transcript of the moment, but they do preserve the phrasing of the swearing-in, such as the line that the Xia house was guilty and that he feared Heaven and dared not leave the wrong unrighted, and they are the most direct material for studying how the Shang side explained this war to itself. As for Jie's conduct on the field, the record keeps only the gestures of flight, and neither his formation nor even whether he was struck by an arrow survives anywhere.
kits: 先說清楚一件容易誤讀的事：卡面上的這把埃及長矛（Egyptian spear）並沒有出現在鳴條的戰場上。它是尼羅河流域早王朝時期的兵器，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上，埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地；它與鳴條之戰的關係，不在某一份戰役的兵器清單裡，而在技術譜系。鳴條陣上真正使用的是東亞自己的冷兵器：最普遍的是青銅矛，矛頭裝在木柲上，格柲護手，與埃及長矛在結構上同屬「金屬矛頭加長杆」這一類；此外有青銅戈，援部有鋒，裝在有柲的長柄上，鉤啄並用，是夏商戰陣上砍殺的主要兵器；再有鉞，既是兵器，也是統軍與賞罰的象徵；弓矢以竹木為身、骨石為鏃，負責接戰前的壓制；盾以木為心，外蒙皮革。車是這場戰爭的關鍵：史載桀「奔車走」，說明夏軍有車，商軍用車亦不例外，殷墟車馬坑所見的雙輪單軸、一車三人的商代戰車架構，正是夏商之交這一技術世代的樣子，而二里頭遺址發現的車轍痕跡，把中原用車的年代往前推到夏代晚期。馬匹在中原的運用此時已進入日常，挽車與乘騎並行。至於攻城器與投石機，鳴條是野戰而非圍城，沒有這類裝備的記載。
kitsEn: One point has to be made first, because it is easy to misread it: the Egyptian spear on the card was not present on the field of Mingtiao. It was a weapon of the Nile valley in the Old Kingdom, a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold city walls and later to recover lost ground. Its relation to the battle of Mingtiao lies not in any battle order of arms but in a line of technique. What was actually used at Mingtiao were the cold weapons of East Asia. The commonest was the bronze spear, its head fitted to a wooden shaft with a guard, and in structure it belongs to the same family as the Egyptian spear, a metal head on a long shaft. Alongside it was the bronze ge, with a bladed upper extension and a socketed tang, mounted on a long shaft and used both to hook and to strike, the principal cutting weapon in Xia and Shang battle lines. There was also the yue, an axe that was at once a weapon and the emblem of command and of reward and punishment. Bows and arrows, bamboo and wood with bone and stone heads, handled the pressure before contact. Shields were wood with leather stretched over them. The chariot was the pivot of this war: the record that Jie fled by chariot and on foot shows that the Xia army had chariots, and the Shang used them as well, the two-wheeled, single-axled car with three men to a team that the chariot pits at Yinxu preserve being of just this technological generation, while the wheel ruts found at the Erlitou site push the use of the chariot in the Central Plain back into the late Xia. Horses were by then in ordinary use there, harnessed to the cars and ridden alike. As for siege engines and stone-throwers, Mingtiao was a battle in the open field and not an investment of a city, and there is no record of such equipment.
tactics: 鳴條之戰的作戰過程，現存文獻留下的只有骨架，而骨架恰好可以看出三段式的結構。第一段是進軍與接戰：湯在翦除葛、韋、顧、昆吾等方國之後率諸侯聯軍東出，兵鋒壓向夏的腹心；夏軍迎戰於鳴條之野，一說是湯的聯軍在一次會戰中即壓垮夏軍，一說是首戰之後夏軍退保三皐，湯再追而戰於鳴條之野。《史記·夏本紀》記「桀走保三皐，湯追之戰於鳴條之野」，把追擊戰放在同一個地名之下，說明戰場是同一片。第二段是崩潰與追擊：史載桀「奔車走」，夏軍的潰散不是被包圍而瓦解，而是在野戰的正面接觸中被衝垮，車兵在這一點上最吃虧——車的衝力依賴速度與縱列，一旦前隊擾亂，後車無處可轉。第三段是收束：湯放桀於南巢，桀數年後死於南巢，湯即天子位，改亳為都，開始了商朝的統治。文獻只留下「奔」「走」「追」「放」幾個動詞，兵形、陣位、進攻次序都沒有記載，因此可以確定的戰術事實只有三條：出戰前商已改易正朔與車服並集結諸侯聯軍；戰役在夏的腹心野地進行，沒有圍城；追擊戰在距離三皐不遠的同一片原野上打完，勝方靠車兵與步兵的正面壓力把對方打到失去戰鬥意志。
tacticsEn: The course of the battle at Mingtiao has survived in the texts as a skeleton, and that skeleton is enough to show a structure in three movements. The first is the advance and the engagement. After cutting away the polities of Ge, Wei, Gu and Kunwu, Tang led the allied host of lords eastward and pressed towards the heart of Xia; the Xia army met him in the field at Mingtiao, some accounts holding that the Shang coalition broke the Xia in a single meeting, and others that the Xia fell back to hold San Gao after the first clash, with Tang pursuing and fighting again in the open country of Mingtiao. The Shiji in the annals of the House of Xia records that Jie fled to hold San Gao and that Tang pursued and fought at the field of Mingtiao, which places the pursuit battle under the same place-name and tells us that it was the same stretch of country. The second movement is the collapse and the pursuit. The record has Jie flying by chariot and on foot: the Xia army was not broken by being surrounded and reduced but was crushed in the open by contact, and the chariot troops were worst placed in this respect, since the shock of a chariot depends on speed and on the order of the column, and when the leading teams are disordered the cars behind have nowhere to turn. The third movement is the closing of the affair. Tang sent Jie into exile at Nanchao, where Jie died some years later according to the Bamboo Annals, and Tang took the throne, made Bo his capital and began the rule of the Shang. The texts preserve only the verbs of flight, of going, of pursuing and of exiling; the formations, the positions and the order of attack are all lost, and so only three tactical facts can be stated with certainty: before the campaign the Shang had corrected the calendar and the dress of the court and had assembled a coalition of lords; the battle was fought in the open country of the Xia heartland and involved no siege; and the pursuit was fought out on the same fields a short march from San Gao, the victory coming from the frontal pressure of chariots and foot, which drove the other side to the point of losing the will to fight.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是文獻自述。年，《史記·夏本紀》與《竹書紀年》一系的傳統紀年把商湯代夏繫在公元前1766年，而近年學界多採夏商斷代工程所定的公元前1600年前後一系，本卡所採的公元前1675年屬年代學修正後的選項之一，至今無定論。月，現存文獻沒有留下鳴條之戰的月份，卡面月份只能按缺略處理，不能反推季節。戰役次數，《孟子·滕文公下》記「湯始征自葛，十一征而無敵於天下」，說的是湯征伐的總數，連同葛、韋、顧、昆吾等方國都在內。夏的統治年數，《史記·夏本紀》列禹至桀凡十七世，《竹書紀年》一系則作四百七十餘年，說法不一。第二類是地理與考古數字。鳴條的地望，《史記集解》引皇甫謐說安邑在河東解縣北，鳴條在其西；地記一類的書說三皐在霍州東三十里，也就是今山西霍州一帶，而山西夏縣、萬榮一帶的考古發掘則在二里頭文化與汾河流域的地面上找尋與之相對應的痕跡；商都亳的所在有商丘、偃師等數說。器物方面，殷墟車馬坑所出商代戰車為雙輪單軸，通常乘三人；二里頭遺址發現的車轍痕跡，把中原用車的年代推前到夏代晚期。第三類只能存疑：兩軍的兵力與車乘數目，後世類書所引《帝王世紀》一系的編年敘述雖曾附會數目，但各本文字互異，無一可作信史；史家只能從「奔車走」一語推知車在軍中的份量，而無法給出具體數字。戰果方面，可確定的是夏朝就此覆亡、桀被放逐於南巢；具體傷亡數字不見於當時記載。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is what the texts say of themselves. The year: the traditional chronology of the Shiji in the annals of the House of Xia and of the Bamboo Annals ties the replacement of Xia by Shang to 1766 BC, while most recent scholarship adopts a date around 1600 BC on the lines laid down by the Xia-Shang Chronology Project, and the 1675 BC used on this card is one of the options produced by the corrected chronologies; there is still no agreement. The month: no surviving text gives the month of the battle of Mingtiao, and the month on the card can only be filled in as a convention, since the season cannot be deduced. The number of campaigns: the Mengzi at Tengwen records that Tang began his campaigns at Ge and in eleven campaigns had no enemy left under heaven, which is a count of the campaigns, including the polities of Ge, Wei, Gu and Kunwu among them. The length of Xia rule: the Shiji in the annals of the House of Xia lists seventeen generations from Yu to Jie, while the Bamboo Annals and its line give a little over four hundred and seventy years, and the accounts differ. The second class is geographical and archaeological. The site of Mingtiao: the Jiji to the Shiji quotes Huangfu Mi to the effect that Anyi lay north of Jie county in Hedong, with Mingtiao to the west of it, and the regional gazetteers put San Gao about thirty li east of Huozhou, that is in the neighbourhood of modern Huozhou in Shanxi; archaeological work in the Xia county and Wanyong area of Shanxi has been looking in the ground of the Erlitou culture and of the Fen valley for traces to match. The site of the Shang capital at Bo has several proposals, among them Shangqiu and Yanshi. The third part of this class is objects: the Shang chariots from the chariot pits at Yinxu have two wheels on a single axle and usually three men to a car, and the wheel ruts at Erlitou carry the use of the chariot in the Central Plain back to the late Xia. The third class can only be doubted. As for the strength of the two armies and the number of cars, the chronological narratives in the class-books that quote the Diwang Shiji did attach figures to the matter, but the wording differs from copy to copy and none of it can serve as history. From the single phrase about fleeing by chariot one can infer the part played by the chariot in the army, but no concrete number can be given. As for the result, what is certain is that the Xia dynasty ended there and that Jie was exiled to Nanchao; there are no casualty figures of the period.
cause: 打起來的原因，後世的說法幾乎都收在一句話裡：夏失其德，天命轉移。往細處拆，可以分成三層。最表層是夏末的政治崩壞：桀寵信妺喜與佞臣，好酒色、崇鬼神、疏忠諫，關龍逢因進諫被殺，豬存子等忠言不被聽；《尚書·湯誓》一系把夏的罪狀列成「有夏多罪，天命殛之」的式樣，《左傳·昭公四年》引述夏王好鬼神的舊事，把荒淫與昏聵連到亡國上。統治層的作為把方國與部落推成敵人，《詩經·商頌·長發》以「受小球大球，為下國綴旒」追述湯的功業，說明這場勝利在商人的敘事裡從來不只是武力的結果，也意味著方國秩序的重新分配，而商族本來就在夏的秩序中居於從屬地位。中層是商的崛起與伊尹的治政：湯以亳為基地，任用伊尹整飭內部、經營盟國，先後翦除夏的方國衛星，把政治影響從商丘、豫東一帶推到晉南，最後才有能力在夏的家門內作戰。第三層是當時整個中原的技術條件：車馬、銅器、弓箭、築城都已經成熟，任何一個部族都能以聯軍形式挑戰王朝，商湯並非以舉國之力孤注一擲，而是用聯盟與速度換取勝機。於是「以臣伐君」「以小邦伐大邦」在鳴條變成可行，而且是可複製的樣本，此後每一次王朝更替，人們都會拿鳴條去比照。
causeEn: Later writers have gathered the reason for the war into a single sentence: Xia had lost its virtue and the Mandate had moved. Taken apart, it lies in three layers. The outermost is the political collapse of the late Xia. Jie favoured You Xi and his flatterers, indulged in wine and women, clung to sorcery and ghosts and shut out those who remonstrated; Guan Longfeng was killed for his remonstrance, and the pleas of men such as Zhu Cunzi were not heard. The Tang Oath in the Shangshu sets out the crimes of Xia in the form of a formula to the effect that the Xia house had many sins and the Mandate would destroy it, and the Zuo Zhuan at Zhao, four, cites the old stories of Xia kings who loved ghosts and spirits, tying intemperance and benightedness to the ruin of the state. The conduct of the rulers drove the polities and tribes into enmity. The Shijing's Shang Odes in the Changfa, with the line about receiving the small and the great jade beads and stringing the princes of the lesser states, recount the achievement of Tang and show that this victory in the narration of the Shang people was never the result of force alone but also a redistribution of the order of the polities, and that the Shang themselves had always stood in a subject position within the Xia order. The middle layer is the rise of the Shang and the government of Yi Yin. Tang used Bo as his base, took Yi Yin into his service, put his own house in order, worked upon his alliances, and cut away in turn the satellite states of Xia, carrying the political influence of the Shang from the region of Shangqiu and eastern Henan into southern Shanxi, and only then had the strength to fight inside Xia's own gate. The deepest layer is the technical conditions of the Central Plain at the time: chariot and horse, bronze casting, the bow and the building of walls were all mature, and any one people could challenge a dynasty in coalition form. Tang was not staking the whole nation on a single throw; he was buying his victory with alliance and speed. It was thus that striking from below at the sovereign, the small state against the great, became feasible at Mingtiao, and it became a model that could be copied, so that after that every change of dynasty was measured against Mingtiao.
impact: 鳴條之後，中國早期王朝的運作方式被改寫了幾件事。第一是政權交接的模式：湯放桀於南巢而代之以天子位，商人自此把「有德者受命」寫成制度性的說法，《尚書·禹貢》與《湯誓》一系以及《孟子》「湯始征自葛，十一征而無敵於天下」的敘述，把革命的路線說成「先征方國、後伐王朝」的長期過程，這條路線此後被周人完整複製。第二是用人與制度的樣板：伊尹在商初的地位確立了「宰相」作為一種制度角色的原型，後世論商必提湯與伊尹的關係；《史記·殷本紀》記湯「改正朔、易服色、上白」，改曆法、改車服、改朝會時辰，等於一次行政與象徵體系的全面換血，而「改正朔」的做法此後在每次改朝換代時都重演一次。第三是暴力規模與戰爭形態的示範：鳴條不是以城牆攻防取勝，而是以聯軍在野地的會戰取勝，車兵與步兵的正面衝撞決定一切，這與數百年後的牧野同屬一個戰爭譜系，後世兵家講「合於諸侯」、講「以義伐」時，援引的多半是這一類先例。第四是考古與文獻的落點：夏的物質面貌在二里頭遺址（河南偃師，年代約在公元前十八至十六世紀之間）被一點點拼出來，早商青銅器則散見於鄭州商城與偃師商城一線的早商地層；因為鳴條本身沒有留下戰場遺存，戰役的具體細節只能靠後世文獻追補，這也說明這場戰爭在史學上更多是一個象徵與起點，而不是一段可精確復原的過程。第五是對「夏」這一名號的影響：夏作為王朝名號被記錄下來，此後的商、周都把自己放在「承夏」的位置上，中國早期王朝序列的觀念由此成形。
impactEn: After Mingtiao, several things about the way the earliest Chinese dynasties worked were rewritten. First, the pattern of the transfer of power. Tang sent Jie into exile at Nanchao and took the place of Heaven as Son of the dynasty, and from then on the Shang wrote the rule of the virtuous into an institutional formula. The Yu Gong and the Tang Shi of the Shangshu and the Mengzi's line about Tang beginning his campaigns at Ge and in eleven campaigns having no enemy left under heaven present the revolutionary road as a long process of first campaigning against the lesser polities and only afterwards striking at the dynasty, and the Zhou copied that road in full. Second, the model for employing men and for institutions: the position held by Yi Yin at the beginning of the Shang established the chancellor as the prototype of an institutional role, and later ages always spoke of the early Shang through the relation between Tang and Yi Yin; the record in the Shiji in the annals of the House of Yin that Tang corrected the calendar, changed the dress of the court and made white the colour above was a wholesale change of the administrative and symbolic system, and the practice of correcting the calendar was repeated at every change of dynasty thereafter. Third, a demonstration of the scale of violence and of the form of war. Mingtiao was not won by fighting against walls but by a coalition meeting in the open field, where the frontal shock of chariot and foot decided everything; it belongs to the same lineage of war as Muye four centuries later, and the military writers who spoke of combining with the lords and of punishing by righteousness were invoking precedents of that kind. Fourth, the archaeological and documentary setting. The material face of Xia has been pieced together little by little at the Erlitou site in Yanshi, Henan, whose phase is dated between roughly the eighteenth and sixteenth centuries BC, and the early Shang bronzes are scattered through the early Shang levels at the Zhengzhou and Yanshi cities. Because Mingtiao itself left no trace of a battlefield, the details of the battle can only be supplied from later texts, which also shows that in history this war is more a symbol and a starting point than a process that can be exactly reconstructed. Fifth, the effect on the name Xia itself. Xia was recorded as the name of a dynasty, and from then on the Shang and Zhou placed themselves in the position of continuing Xia, and the idea of a sequence of early Chinese dynasties took shape.
result: 公元前1675年，鳴條之野的會戰以夏軍的全面崩潰告終。《史記·夏本紀》記桀「走保三皐」，湯追之再戰於鳴條之野，桀「奔車走」，軍隊在野地接觸中被壓垮；湯隨即放桀於南巢，桀數年後死於南巢，《竹書紀年》一系記桀被放於南巢三年而死。湯即位為天子，改亳為都，商朝由此開始，此後經盤庚遷殷、到帝辛亡國，歷時約五百三十年，是信史時代第一個可考的王朝。從戰爭本身看，可以確定的事只有四條：出戰的是商湯的諸侯聯軍，夏桀的中央軍隊在野戰中崩潰；戰役發生在夏的腹心地帶，不在夏都城牆之下，因此不存在圍城與攻城；車兵在夏軍的潰敗中扮演了關鍵角色，否則不會有「奔車走」的記載；戰後夏桀本人並未當場戰死，而是被放逐安置。有一點必須說明：這場戰爭的具體經過幾乎全部出自戰國至漢初文人的追述，沒有任何一份戰當時的記錄流傳下來，因此它的具體兵力、陣形與戰損都不可考，只能說明結構——一次由方國聯盟完成的、以野戰會勝取決的王朝更替。往後每次有諸侯問鼎、每次王朝邊界被爭奪，最先被想起的仍然是鳴條這個地名。
resultEn: In 1675 BC the meeting in the field at Mingtiao ended with the total collapse of the Xia army. The Shiji in the annals of the House of Xia records that Jie fled to hold San Gao and that Tang pursued and fought again at the field of Mingtiao, and that Jie fled by chariot and on foot, his army crushed in contact in the open country. Tang then sent him into exile at Nanchao, where he died some years later, the Bamboo Annals recording that Jie was let go at Nanchao and died after three years. Tang took the throne, made Bo his capital, and the Shang dynasty began; it lasted about five hundred and thirty years through the move of Pan Geng to Yin down to the fall of Di Xin, and it is the first dynasty of the documented age. As to the war itself, only four things can be stated with certainty: the force that marched was a coalition of lords under Tang; the central Xia troops broke up in a battle fought in the open; the fight took place in the heartland of Xia and not beneath the walls of the Xia capital, so there was no siege and no storming of a city; and the chariot played a decisive part in the rout of the Xia, otherwise the record of flight by chariot and on foot would not stand. One thing must be said plainly: almost the whole course of this battle comes from the retrospective narratives of writers of the Warring States and the early Han, and no record of the moment itself has come down to us, so its strength, its formations and its losses cannot be made out. What can be said is the structure, a change of dynasty carried out by an alliance of polities and decided by a pitched meeting in the open field. And whenever the lords in later ages have asked after the throne, and whenever the borders of a dynasty have been fought over, the first name to be recalled has still been Mingtiao.
